name: מֹשֶׁה
gloss: drawing out; named for being drawn out of the water
summary: Moses the Levite, son of Amram and Jochebed and brother of Aaron and Miriam, through whom Yahweh brought Israel out of Egypt and gave the law; the New Testament calls him Μωϋσῆς. Pharaoh’s daughter named him, “for out of the water I drew him” (מְשִׁיתִהוּ), from the verb מָשָׁה “draw out”. The form is that of the verb’s active participle, “one drawing out”: the child drawn out of the river became the one through whom Yahweh drew his people out of the sea (Isa 63:11–12).

evidence.note: וַתִּקְרָא שְׁמוֹ מֹשֶׁה וַתֹּאמֶר כִּי מִן־הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ: the naming and its reason.
Amram took Jochebed, and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
The root’s verb again: Yahweh יַמְשֵׁנִי מִמַּיִם רַבִּים, “drew me out of many waters”.
“Then he remembered the days of old, Moses, his people: where is he who brought them up out of the sea?”: the name set beside bringing up out of water.
Moses declared the appointed feasts of Yahweh to the sons of Israel.
When the ark set out, Moses said, “Rise up, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered.”
“My servant Moses … in all my house he is faithful.”
No prophet arose again in Israel like Moses, whom Yahweh knew face to face.
The Aramaic: as it is written in the book of Moses.
Stephen retells the birth, the setting out and Pharaoh’s daughter taking him up as her son.
Hid by his parents three months; grown, he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.

note: bdb: m.ds.ab is the Hebrew name, xm.am.ab the Aramaic (Ezr 6:18); the database counts the same tokens under both. The participle form “one drawing out” is a reading of the vowels (as רֹעֶה, עֹשֶׂה); Exo 2:10 gives the reason for the name without saying whether it is active or passive. An Egyptian source (msi̯ “give birth”, ms “child”) is discussed in the root entry’s note; against it, scripture explains the name from Hebrew, and it writes Egyptian -ms- with ס (רַעְמְסֵס), not ש. TIPNR lists מְנַשֶּׁה as a form of Moses for Jdg 18:30, where the text has a suspended nun; that token is filed under Manasseh and is not counted here.
